title: Reusable Portfolio Website Framework
section: The problem: wanting a portfolio, but not knowing how to build one
text:
The problem: wanting a portfolio, but not knowing how to build one
Friends and colleagues wanted their own portfolio websites to present their skills, projects, and professional background. Many could not code or were uncomfortable with basic programming. Building a website from scratch presented a barrier to making their work visible.
This project grew out of that need. I wanted to provide a reusable starting point that would reduce the amount of technical work required and make the process easier to understand.

title: Reusable Portfolio Website Framework
text:
My approach
I developed a portfolio framework around a consistent set of pages: an introduction, biography, projects, research, notes, CV, and contact information. The structure gives users a place for their material before they have to make decisions about layout or navigation.
The implementation uses Quarto, Markdown, and CSS. Content lives in editable source files, while the shared configuration and stylesheet provide navigation and a consistent appearance. A project template provides a repeatable structure for explaining the question, data, methods, findings, and limitations of new work.

title: Reusable Portfolio Website Framework
text:
Making reuse practical
The project combines the website with guidance for maintaining it:

Reusable page and project layouts: a starting structure that can be personalised rather than built again from scratch.
Responsive presentation: layouts that adapt to desktop and smaller screens.
Downloadable materials: a place for a CV and supporting project files.
An editing guide: instructions for changing text, adding projects, replacing images, checking links, and previewing the site.
A documented publishing workflow: editable source and generated website files are kept separate, with deployment through GitHub Pages.

The guide matters as much as the layout. Someone who receives a template also needs to know where their information goes and how to update it later.

title: Reusable Portfolio Website Framework
text:
My contribution
I identified the need through friends and colleagues, shaped the content structure around their use case, supplied the initial portfolio materials, and refined the site and documentation through an iterative build. I used AI assistance for implementation and editing, while directing the project’s purpose and reviewing the result.

title: Reusable Portfolio Website Framework
text:
What the project demonstrates
This work connects a real need with a practical implementation: listening to potential users, defining a repeatable structure, integrating content and presentation, documenting maintenance, and taking a website through deployment.
My own portfolio provides a working example of the approach. The current outcome is a reusable foundation and an editing workflow; I have not measured adoption or time savings among other users.

title: Reusable Portfolio Website Framework
text:
Limits and next improvements
The current framework reduces the need to write website code from scratch. It still requires guided editing of text files and some setup to publish. It is not yet a fully no-code editor.
The next useful step is to observe a friend or colleague personalising a copy, record where they get stuck, and improve the instructions or editing experience. A guided form or visual editor could further reduce the technical steps, but those features are not part of the current implementation.

The highest-scoring 10% of historical test records contained approximately 45% of all subscribers. The practical question: how could a bank prioritise a limited campaign budget?
Download the analysis notebook

title: Bank Marketing: Smarter Campaign Targeting
text:
Question and data
Can customer information, campaign history, and economic indicators help identify records more likely to correspond to a term-deposit subscription?
The analysis uses UCI Bank Marketing, specifically bank-additional-full.csv: 41,188 records, 20 input variables, and a binary subscription target. The data comes from a Portuguese banking institution’s campaigns between May 2008 and November 2010.
Dataset and documentation

title: Bank Marketing: Smarter Campaign Targeting
text:
Preparing the evidence

Removed 12 exact duplicate copies, leaving 41,176 records. Without customer IDs, identical rows cannot be proven to represent the same individual.
Retained unknown as a categorical value rather than deleting large numbers of observations.
Replaced the special pdays = 999 code with a separate previous-contact indicator and a zero placeholder for days.
Excluded call duration, which is unavailable before a call and would make targeting results unrealistic.

Only 11.27% of remaining records were subscribers. Accuracy alone would therefore reward a model that mostly predicts non-subscription.



Subscription counts: the target is heavily imbalanced.

title: Bank Marketing: Smarter Campaign Targeting
text:
Modelling and evaluation
A stratified random split produced 26,352 training, 6,588 validation, and 8,236 test records: approximately 64%, 16%, and 20% of the cleaned data.
I compared a majority-class baseline, logistic regression, decision trees, and random forests, including class-weighted variants. Numerical scaling was fitted on training data. Model selection and threshold tuning used validation data.
Balanced logistic regression was selected for the recall/F1 trade-off. A threshold of 0.64 maximised validation F1 within the tested range. The model and preprocessing were then refitted on the 80% development set before final holdout evaluation.

The confusion matrix contains 561 true positives, 744 false positives, 367 false negatives, and 6,564 true negatives. At the selected threshold, the model identified about 60% of subscribers, with about 43% of positive predictions corresponding to subscribers.

title: Bank Marketing: Smarter Campaign Targeting
text:
Findings and interpretation
Previous campaign history was a useful signal. Students and retired customers showed higher observed subscription rates than several other occupation groups, although group sizes differed. Contact channel, frequency, campaign timing, and economic conditions also contributed information.



Observed subscription rates by occupation; these are descriptive associations.


These are predictive and descriptive relationships. They do not establish that changing occupation, contact channel, or call frequency would cause higher subscription.

title: Bank Marketing: Smarter Campaign Targeting
text:
Limitations and next steps

Prediction timing: removing duration addresses one major leakage risk. A strict pre-campaign model still needs an availability audit: campaign includes the current contact, and contact timing/channel must be known or planned at scoring time.
Time: the random split mixes historical periods. A chronological evaluation is needed to assess generalisation to later campaigns.
Encoding: dummy encoding was performed separately and aligned to training columns. A fitted encoder and pipeline would make reference categories and handling of unseen categories more robust.
Calibration: class-weighted model scores should not automatically be read as real-world probabilities. The 0.64 cutoff is a decision threshold, not a guaranteed 64% likelihood.
Business value: call costs, deposit value, uncertainty, and prospective testing are needed before recommending deployment.
Scope: these are older records from one banking setting. Results have not been validated on current or Nigerian banking data.

title: Bank Marketing: Smarter Campaign Targeting
text:
Reproduce the analysis
Download the notebook and obtain bank-additional-full.csv from the UCI dataset. Put the CSV beside the notebook. The analysis uses Python, Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, scikit-learn, and Jupyter.

title: Notes
section: Why high accuracy can hide a weak marketing model
text:
Why high accuracy can hide a weak marketing model
In my Bank Marketing analysis, only about 11.3% of records were subscribers. A baseline that always predicted “no” achieved roughly 88.7% validation accuracy while identifying no subscribers.
That changed how I evaluated success. I compared precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, and average precision, then tested how many subscribers appeared in the highest-scoring customer groups. The final ranking placed about 45% of test-set subscribers in the top 10% of records.
The lesson: choose metrics that reflect the decision. For a team with limited call capacity, the concentration of subscribers near the top of a ranking can be more informative than overall accuracy.

title: Economic Data Pipeline & Research Platform
section: The problem: getting from a research question to usable data
text:
The problem: getting from a research question to usable data
Finding an indicator is only the beginning of empirical research. Researchers also need to identify the right country and period, understand definitions, check coverage, organise observations, and retain enough source information to explain where their data came from.
I built an economic data pipeline and research platform to bring these steps into a connected workflow. The project links my Economics background with Data Science and software development, with a practical focus on making economic data easier to discover, inspect, and prepare for research.

title: Economic Data Pipeline & Research Platform
text:
What I built
The project includes a browser-based Streamlit workspace backed by a reusable Python service. Researchers select countries, a year range, and World Bank indicators, then build a dataset they can inspect and download.
The current platform supports annual World Development Indicators. It provides indicator search, research presets, data tables, comparison charts, coverage reports, definitions, and source information. CSV and documented Excel exports let researchers continue their analysis outside the application.

title: Economic Data Pipeline & Research Platform
text:
The research workflow


1. Find relevant indicators
Search country and indicator catalogues by name, code, or definition. Choose a period and customise the selected indicators.


2. Retrieve and inspect
Retrieve series through the World Bank API, validate observations, and examine coverage, charts, and missing values.


3. Export with context
Download a research dataset alongside source dates, indicator definitions, settings, and suggested citations.

title: Economic Data Pipeline & Research Platform
section: Engineering decisions that support research reliability
text:
Engineering decisions that support research reliability

Validate inputs and observations: check country and indicator identity, year ranges, unique years, and finite numeric values.
Preserve missing information: retain gaps in annual series and charts. Missing observations are not filled, interpolated, or replaced with zero.
Separate missing data from retrieval failures: display partial failures explicitly and retry failed series while retaining successful observations.
Track provenance: retain original indicator codes, source URLs, retrieval timestamps, API update dates, and available provider metadata.
Use validated caches: cache responses with a 24-hour lifetime, schema information, identity checks, and checksums. Expired matching caches may be used during API failure, with a visible stale-data label.
Keep exports separate from original data: generate CSV and Excel downloads in memory rather than overwriting existing processed datasets.

These choices help a researcher see both the available evidence and the conditions under which it was retrieved. Checksums detect accidental corruption; they do not prove source authenticity.

title: Economic Data Pipeline & Research Platform
text:
Architecture and implementation
Interface: Streamlit manages selection, retrieval progress, result views, and session state.
Backend: a Python service handles API requests, pagination, caching, validation, dataset assembly, coverage, and exports.
Research presentation: a separate module provides presets, charts, readable coverage summaries, and citation/settings output.
The backend is separate from Streamlit and performs no work on import. The application also separates selection controls from result views so that changing a selection does not silently replace an existing result.
The repository includes deterministic tests for backend behaviour and Streamlit flows, including invalid observations, cache corruption, stale fallback, partial failures, missing values, and exports. This portfolio summary is based on inspection of the source and documentation; it does not report a new test run or a measured performance improvement.

title: Economic Data Pipeline & Research Platform
text:
Scope and limitations
The current data source is World Bank World Development Indicators, rather than a general connection to every economic database. Regional and income aggregates and other World Bank datasets are outside the current scope.
Historical data may be revised by its provider. Researchers should retain their downloaded datasets, definitions, and retrieval dates. Caches are an optimisation and may disappear after a hosting restart.
The repository also contains original command-line tools and an offline archive viewer. Legacy archive files are labelled separately because they do not have verified API retrieval provenance.

title: Economic Data Pipeline & Research Platform
text:
